outcome: The general Tutte 4-flow conjecture (every bridgeless Petersen-minor-free graph has a nowhere-zero 4-flow) remains open, but two genuine sub-cases were settled in the window: (1) the cubic-graph restriction of the conjecture, equivalent to Tutte's three-edge-coloring conjecture, was completed by a July/August 2026 preprint proving the last outstanding 'apex' case (combined with the pre-2024 doublecross case), and (2) a July 2026 preprint proved the 4-flow property for the strictly smaller class of graphs excluding a proper minor of the Petersen graph (the P/e-minor-free case). Both are preprints, not yet digested by the expert community.

ai.basis_quote: GitHub Copilot was used to assist in implementing parts of the authors' verification software. All generated code was reviewed by the authors. ... ChatGPT Pro and Gemini Deep Think were also used to assist with exposition and to review the consistency between the mathematical descriptions and the pseudocode. ... independent implementations were reconstructed by ChatGPT Pro and Claude Code, directly from the pseudocode ... without access to the authors' source code. Both independently reproduced the computational results required in this paper. These reconstructions are not part of the mathematical justification of the theorem, but provide additional evidence for the reproducibility of the computations.

summary: The stated bullet is the general Tutte 4-flow conjecture: every bridgeless graph with no Petersen-graph minor has a nowhere-zero 4-flow. Both the arXiv preprint the openproblemgarden.org survey page (accessed 2026-09-22) confirm the general conjecture is still open. Within the 26 Jan 2024–present window, two case results were established, both remaining unread by the wider expert community. (a) Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Matsuo, Miyashita, Mohar & Sonobe, 'Three-edge-coloring apex cubic graphs' (arXiv:2608.22870, submitted 24 Aug 2026), prove the 'apex' case of the reduction Robertson–Seymour–Thomas set up for the cubic-graph restriction of the conjecture (which for cubic graphs is equivalent, via 3-edge-colorability, to Tutte's three-edge-coloring conjecture). The 'doublecross' case was already settled by Edwards–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas (2014/2016), which predates the window, so the only new event in the window is the apex case, completing the cubic special case. This is a genuine case of the bullet (cubic graphs are a restriction of 'bridgeless Petersen-minor-free graphs'), so it counts as `partial`, not a resolution of the general conjecture. The proof is computer-assisted (in the manner of the Four Color Theorem) and, as of this writing (~1 month after posting), has not been digested by an independent expert reviewer or accepted at a venue of record — an automated 'Pith Review' site flags that the computational/'cartwheel-search' part needs independent audit — so status is not yet `resolved`, though I am recording it as `partial` (a case was settled) rather than `claimed` because the case in question (cubic apex graphs) is itself fully specified and the reduction to it is an established, previously-published structural result; only the final case's verification is unreviewed. Readers should treat the cubic case as not-yet-fully-vetted. (b) Pintér, 'Nowhere-zero 4-flows in graphs excluding a proper minor of the Petersen graph' (arXiv:2607.22267, v1 24 Jul 2026, v2 9 Aug 2026), proves the 4-flow property for the class of graphs excluding P/e (Petersen graph with one edge contracted) as a minor. The paper's own introduction establishes that Q(=P/e)-minor-free graphs form a strictly smaller class than Petersen-minor-free graphs (Ex(Q) ⊊ ... in the minor order, i.e. excluding a minor of Petersen is a stronger restriction than excluding Petersen itself), so this is also a genuine, smaller case of the bullet, not a distinct/variant problem — I disagree with the triage's uncertainty on this point (see triage_disagreement). On AI: the apex-cubic paper explicitly discloses generative-AI use (GitHub Copilot for verification-software implementation, reviewed by the authors; ChatGPT Pro and Gemini Deep Think for exposition/consistency checking; and, notably, ChatGPT Pro and Claude Code used to independently reconstruct the verification code from pseudocode alone as a reproducibility check) — but the authors explicitly state these reconstructions 'are not part of the mathematical justification of the theorem.' No AI system produced any mathematics that appears in the theorem or proof; all AI use is checking/coding/exposition assistance, so ai_role is `none` per the rubric. The Pintér paper discloses using ChatGPT and Claude 'for literature research, editorial assistance, and help writing the accompanying code' for its finite (Python/Zenodo-archived) verification script — again none of this produced mathematics that appears in the result, so ai_role is `none` there as well.
competing_reading: One could argue the apex-cubic result, since it completes an entire named sub-conjecture (Tutte's three-edge-coloring conjecture) rather than merely narrowing a search space, deserves `resolved` status for that sub-conjecture even though the parent bullet (the full 4-flow conjecture) stays `partial`/open. I did not adopt this because the schema's `status` field tracks the bullet as given, and because the proof is a very recent (Aug 2026), computer-assisted preprint with no located expert digestion yet — under §6.1 an unreviewed computer-assisted certificate should be `claimed` rather than `resolved` even when it fully settles a sub-conjecture. A stricter reading could therefore call the cubic-case event `claimed` rather than folding it into `partial`; I chose `partial` because a `partial` status is about the parent bullet only having a piece settled, and that piece (the cubic restriction) rests on a currently-unreviewed proof, which the summary flags explicitly.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (e.g. a referee report, a Robertson/Seymour/Thomas-adjacent commentary, or acceptance at a journal/conference of record) of arXiv:2608.22870's proof and its computer-assisted verification would move the cubic-graph case from an unreviewed preprint to a properly vetted result. For the general bullet itself, only a resolution of the full Petersen-minor-free case (not restricted to cubic or to Q-minor-free graphs) would move status past `partial`.
